key_insight: A 2026 public charge rule could reduce immigrants’ use of primary care in NYC and increase premature mortality, especially over the long term.
clinical_relevance: Health systems and policymakers should anticipate reduced coverage/care-seeking among immigrant communities and plan outreach to protect access to primary care.
method: Deterministic compartmental simulation using ordinary differential equations (ODEs).
Inputs from 2023 NYC vital statistics and American Community Survey data.
Scenario modeling of conservative, moderate, and aggressive avoidance/disenrollment (“chilling effect”) with projected outcomes over 5 and 20 years.
evidence_signal: The model estimated 4.1% to 9.9% lower primary care access, 5.1% to 12.2% fewer doctor visits, and 4.4% to 17.4% higher premature mortality depending on scenario.
watch_item: This is a simulation based on prior effect estimates, so real-world impact depends on how strongly the rule changes behavior and whether local protections reduce the chilling effect.
paper_title: The 2026 public charge rule and long-term health impacts among NYC immigrants: a simulation study
